chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked, while I was present, about a man who revived dead land, dug a canal in it, built houses, and planted palm trees and trees.

So he said: "It belongs to him, and he is entitled to the rent of its houses. And upon him in it is the tenth for what is watered by the sky, or the flood of a valley, or a spring; and upon him, for what is watered by water-lifting devices and the bucket, is half of the tenth."

key_terms.أَجْرُ بُيُوتِهَا: the rent or yield of the houses built on the land
key_terms.أَحْيَا: brought into use by reviving and cultivating
key_terms.أَرْضًا مَوَاتًا: dead or barren land without prior cultivation or productive use
key_terms.نَهْرًا: a canal or watercourse dug for irrigation
key_terms.نِصْفُ ٱلْعُشْرِ: half of one-tenth due on produce irrigated through effort and tools
key_terms.ٱلْعُشْرُ: one-tenth due on produce irrigated naturally
key_terms.ٱلْغَرْبُ: the large bucket used to draw water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reviving dead land and the tenth due on its produce in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on reviving barren land: the one who brings dead land into productive use becomes entitled to it and to the proceeds of what he builds on it. It also sets the zakat-related agricultural due according to the method of irrigation, distinguishing between naturally watered land and land irrigated through labor and devices.
